author: Oya Canli

english.title: Grease: The Immersive Movie Musical ? My Review
english.body:
Grease has always had a very special place in my heart. It was the first musical I ever saw, and I fell in love with it immediately. I have also been a huge fan of the movie for years, so when I heard about Grease: The Immersive Movie Musical in London, I knew I had to go.

I went to Evolution London in Battersea Park expecting to see Grease in a completely different way, the first thing that impressed me was the transformation of the venue. Turning such a huge space into the world of Rydell High was a brilliant idea. Walking into the venue felt like entering the universe of Grease rather than simply going to see a show. The different areas, the atmosphere, the costumes, the music and the performers all helped create that feeling.

What I loved most was I saw older generations dressed as Pink Ladies, people wearing Sandy-inspired outfits and T-Bird jackets, and fans of all ages completely embracing the world of Grease. I found that incredibly heartwarming. I loved seeing people who have probably loved this movie for decades dressing up and enjoying themselves just as much as younger fans. For me, that made the experience feel even more special.

I also really enjoyed seeing the movie combined with live performers. Watching the familiar scenes on the screen while actors performed around us created some wonderful moments. I already know all of the songs and scenes by heart, so seeing them happening around me in this environment was great fun.

At the same time, I realised that I actually prefer seeing Grease as a traditional musical. Because I love Grease so much, I found myself sometimes wanting to concentrate completely on the live performers and the story. With the immersive format, there is so much happening around me and the original movie is still such a big part of the experience that I occasionally found myself wishing I could simply sit down and watch the actors perform the whole musical on stage.

So, if someone asked me whether I would recommend the immersive experience or a traditional Grease musical, I would personally choose the traditional musical.
But I am still very happy that I experienced this.

I think the immersive version is especially wonderful for someone who already loves the movie. I got to walk into Rydell High, see people dressed as characters I have known for years, hear the songs I grew up loving and experience the story in a completely different environment.

For me, the most beautiful part was seeing how much Grease still means to people. Looking around and seeing Pink Ladies and Sandys of different generations made me smile. I felt like I was surrounded by people who had all come for the same reason I had: because they simply love Grease.

Grease was very different when it first began. The original musical was created by Jim Jacobs and Warren Casey and first performed in Chicago in 1971. The 1978 film then transformed it into a worldwide phenomenon. Interestingly, some of the songs I know best ? including ?You're the One That I Want? and ?Hopelessly Devoted to You? ? were written specifically for the movie rather than the original stage musical.

The original musical premiered in Chicago in 1971 and was much darker, rougher and more explicit. The T-Birds were originally called the Burger Palace Boys, and the show was much more rooted in Chicago teenage life.

And perhaps the most amazing fact for me is that the 1978 movie was made for around $6 million and went on to become one of the biggest musical-film successes ever.

My verdict: ?????

I would recommend Grease Musical to anyone who loves the movie and wants to step inside its world for an evening.

Grease: The Immersive Movie Musical is at Evolution London, Battersea Park, London, from 22 July to 13 September 2026. The experience combines the original movie with live performers and an immersive recreation of the Grease world. It is worth wearing comfortable shoes and coming ready to walk around, interact and become part of the experience rather than expecting a conventional theatre performance.
